message:
Promotion iteration 2: run the WIG review and the web-quality audit, fix what they found (#184)

* Run the two audits the baseline could not, and fix what they found (promotion iteration 2)

The baseline scored conditions 7 and 8 UNVERIFIED with the reason "not run".
Both are now run, against the surface a user actually gets — the built bundle
served by `vite preview`, not the dev server — with the tool output committed
next to the command that produced it.

They are kept separate on purpose. Condition 8 is decided by Lighthouse 13.4.1
and @axe-core/cli 4.13.0. Condition 7 is a review of the Vercel Web Interface
Guidelines, fetched live, written up finding by finding in promotion/WIG_REVIEW.md,
each one citing a measurement or a screenshot. A Lighthouse score is not a WIG
review and cannot stand in for one; promotion/run-web-audits.mjs takes the
measurements the review needs and says so in its header, but it does not perform
the review.

What the audits found, and what changed:

- Three composer controls indicated focus only on the shared composer, which is
  already lit by the time focus reaches them — so tabbing brief -> model ->
  effort changed nothing on screen. The baseline called this "no visible focus
  indicator", which was too strong and missed the worse behaviour: reading only
  the focused element's own computed style cannot see a group ring. Both
  `outline: 0` declarations are deleted, so the existing global
  `:where(:focus-visible)` ring applies — it never fired because `:where()`
  contributes zero specificity. 10 of 13 stops with their own ring -> 13 of 13.
- The file input had no accessible name: axe `label`, impact critical, and the
  sole reason Lighthouse accessibility sat at 0.93. axe violations 1 -> 0,
  accessibility 0.93 -> 1.00.
- The brand link's visible text ("N NodeSlide") was not contained in its
  accessible name, so voice control cannot activate it. The mark is drawn by CSS
  now. Reported by Lighthouse and not by @axe-core/cli: same axe-core, different
  default tag sets — running one is not running the audit.
- The brief textarea was 15px and the selects 11px at 390, which makes iOS zoom
  the viewport on focus; the submit button was 40x40 against a 44px floor.

Two majors are found and NOT fixed, with reproductions instead of attempts:
D7, the canvas pager and zoom controls are drawn on top of the presenter-notes
textarea at all three widths (measured rectangles; found by looking at a
screenshot after every automated check on that screen had passed), and D8, a
5.05 MB vendor chunk that puts LCP at 12.6 s on Lighthouse's throttled mobile
profile. Fixing either is a structural change to a surface this iteration did
not otherwise touch.

Scorecard 0/12 -> 6/12 PASS, and no row is UNVERIFIED any more. 4, 5, 6 and 9
pass on measurements of the editor, which the baseline never reached; 3 passes
on six screenshots; 12 passes because every fix here was measured before and
after in the rendered app. 7, 8 and 10 move UNVERIFIED -> FAIL: the audits ran
and found something real that is still open.

scripts/tests/nodeslide-landing-a11y.test.mjs guards the source half with no
browser; reverting any of the four fixes fails 4 of its 7 cases.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(promotion): name every condition the iteration moved, including 12

The entry listed 4, 5, 6, 9 while the scorecard passed 3, 4, 5, 6, 9 and 12.
Two documents disagreeing about which rows moved is exactly the drift the log
exists to prevent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------
